body.statement: Characterize the smallest separation from lower-order or plateau profiles under which one procedure is honest over \(m\in\{1,\ldots,k-1\}\) and attains the corresponding fixed-order representing-model diameter. Under the currently proved full-class modulus this diameter is \(\rho_N^{k/((k+n/2)(m+1))}\); the sharper diameter \(\rho_N^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\) additionally requires an affirmative resolution of \(\mathrm{oeq:full\text{-}incompressible\text{-}rigidity}\). Prove a matching impossibility result below the separation boundary.
body.justification: Unknown critical order is empirically unavoidable, but honest adaptation across nonregular inverse exponents may require an explicit testing margin.
body.gap: Bull and Nickl characterize smoothness adaptation for ordinary \(L^2\) density sets, not adaptation across causal inverse orders or proximity to a nonidentified plateau.
body.consumer: The result would tell practitioners when the critical order can be learned from data, when the proved conservative fixed-order representing-model diameter is attainable adaptively, and when a worst-order radius is unavoidable.

obligation.what_is_open: A numerical separation functional, an honest adaptive test over critical orders, and a matching impossibility theorem below its testing boundary.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen adaptation handle does not define a topology or numerical distance to lower-order and plateau classes, and no minimax testing modulus for those boundaries has been proved. The sharper fixed-order diameter additionally depends on the unresolved full incompressible-rigidity question.
obligation.attempted: The fixed-order spectral law ball, corrected coverage theorem, and proved scalar finite-type modulus yield honest conservative fixed-order representing-model diameters, but these facts do not construct a test of critical order or identify its sharp separation boundary.
obligation.partial_result:
For each fixed known \(m\), Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:quotient\text{-}confidence\text{-}set}\) gives an honest quotient-valued set with representing-model diameter of order
\[
\rho_N^{k/((k+n/2)(m+1))}.
\]
The sharper order
\[
\rho_N^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}
\]
would follow only after an affirmative resolution of \(\mathrm{oeq:full\text{-}incompressible\text{-}rigidity}\). No distance to the union of lower-order classes or to the closure of plateau profiles is defined, so neither an adaptive testing rule nor a matching below-boundary impossibility theorem is determined by the frozen construction.
